context:
Goal: guards stop mistakes Claude is likely to make, and cost less than the harm they stop.
Problem (rule): no record shows a runner dropping `--root`. You said building-guard-needs-incident is a judge of lift, not a hard rule, and asked whether keeping the guard loses nothing. Not quite nothing: (1) main has none of merge_calls, _call_pieces or merge_args_of, so keeping means building them: measured by the lane at 13:2x CST, about 275 added lines of hook code (guard_merge.py +246/-15, guard.py +24/-2, guard_core.py +4/-2) plus 755 test lines; the splitting fix alone is about 50 lines; (2) a guard that wrongly refuses a valid command costs a runner time, and this one's false-refusal rate is still unmeasured: the cloud session has no past runner commands, the real ones are on your computer (guard.log, transcripts). The guard's own 16 allow/refuse test cases are green, which is fixtures, not history. If both are small, keeping loses little and gains a catch for the dropped-root case. The `$( )` splitting fix in #2071 stands alone either way.
Based on (ruling): your words 11:53 CST Nov 13 (that rule is a lift judge); decision guard-that-cries-wolf-is-spent.
Departs from: main — main has no such guard; b or c adds it.

options.how: Drop the guard. Main has no splitting code the fix could change, so #2071 closes after the ledger.
options.label: Drop the guard; nothing else to build
options.lose: A runner that drops `--root` is not caught.

options.how: Rebuild the guard on #1811, with its three helper pieces.
options.label: Keep the guard as the lane proposes
options.lose: Build effort and an unmeasured false-refusal rate.

options.gain: The choice rests on a measure, not a guess.
options.how: A session on your computer replays past runner merge commands (guard.log, transcripts) through the #2071 head (ref split-and-in-subst) and reports the false refusals; the build is already measured at about 275 lines. No false refusals means keep, else drop.
options.label: Keep it only if a replay shows no false refusals and the build is small (recommended)
options.lose: One extra step on your computer before #2071 closes or merges; the cloud cannot run it.

reply: 13:30 CST. Your 11:53 CST note on 715 was a question, not a pick: if we keep the guard, do we lose nothing? Answer: almost nothing. The build is about 275 hook lines, and the guard's own 16 test cases pass. Still unmeasured: whether it wrongly refuses a real command. Only your computer holds those past commands, and no session on it is reachable from here. So I need your pick: a (drop it), b (keep it), or c (keep it if a replay shows no false refusals). Lane runner-repos-in-parallel is waiting on this item.

shown.label: Drop the guard; nothing else to build
Keep the guard as the lane proposes
Keep it only if a replay shows no false refusals and the build is small (recommended)

title: Keep the guard merge-roots-cover from PR #2071 if it costs little, or drop it and keep only the command-splitting fix?
